paragraphs: Amar hakkatub: "vehaya bayyom hashshishshi vehekinu et asher yabiu". veameru rabbotenu zikronam libraka: nirmaz kan shene debarim baasiyyat tzareke shabbat bayyom hashshishshi; haechad hu, sheyyaaseh tzareke shabbat besimcha, sheddareshu: en "vehaya" ella leshon simcha; vehashsheni, shetztzarik laasot bizrizut lehashkim babboqer lehakin tzareke shabbat, shenneemar: "vehaya bayyom hashshishshi vehekinu", en "vehaya" ella miyyad, shenneemar: "vehaya ki qam happelishti", kelomar, kesheyyihyeh yom hashshishshi beshacharit yakinu letzareke shabbat; vkm"sh mera"n "b"y" beshem hatanchuma. verabbenu hattur za"l hebi taam acher bechiyyub hahakana bizrizut babboqer, diktib: "vehekinu et asher yabiu", mashma dehahakana tihyeh duvmya dahabaa shehiyyatah babboqer, shenneemar: "vayyilqetu oto babboqer babboqer", umeachar demappeqi lah lizrizut dahakana mittebat "vehaya" shehu leshon miyyad, al ken, ap al gab dead d' shaot chashib boqer, im kol zeh tzarik lehashkim lehaqdim tzareke shabbat bekol mah deepshar. al ken, gam mi sheddarko liqboa bekol yom et lilmod tora achar hattepilla, lo yaaseh qeba zeh beereb shabbat, ella raq yilmod shenayim miqra veechad targum shel parashat hashshabua, veyetze liqnot tzareke shabbat. veim yirtzeh latzet qodem sheyyiqra shenayim miqra veechad targum, kede sheyyelek liqnot bimhera, rashshay, veaach"k yiqra bebeto. veken hamminhag poh irenu bagdad, d"p shellomedim qebiut betalmud tora bekol yom achar hattepilla - en lomedim beereb shabbat velo beereb yv"t.

clarification.explanation: From the verse "And it shall be on the sixth day that they shall prepare what they bring in," the Sages derived two things about preparing the needs of the Sabbath on the sixth day: that one should do so with joy ("vehayah" implies joy), and that one should do so promptly and early in the morning ("vehayah" implies immediacy). Therefore, even one who is accustomed to setting a fixed time for study after prayer should not do so on the eve of the Sabbath, but should instead study Shnayim Mikra veEchad Targum and then go out to buy the needs of the Sabbath (or, if he wishes, buy first and read at home). This is also the custom in Baghdad, where fixed study is not held on the eve of the Sabbath or the eve of a festival.
takeaways: The needs of the Sabbath are prepared with joy and promptly, early on Friday morning
Fixed study is not held on the eve of the Sabbath; one hurries instead to the shopping

paragraphs: Basar vekaddomeh, deqapetzi aleha zebine beereb shabbat, veim yamtin liqnoto ad achar tepilla lo yimtza basar tob, muttar liqnoto qodem tepilla, mishshum dachashib zeh tzorek metzuvveh shel oneg shabbat, ak bitnay shello yebattel tepilla im hatztzibbur, ella yimtza lo kat meucheret sheyyitpallel immahem; veayyen "mishbetzot zahab" vechayye-adam ushear acharonim.

clarification.explanation: Meat and similar items, which many rush to buy on the eve of the Sabbath, such that if one waits until after prayer he will not find good meat — it is permitted to buy it before prayer, since this serves the commandment of delighting in the Sabbath. This is on condition that he not thereby forgo praying with the congregation, but find a later minyan to pray with.
takeaways: It is permitted to buy good meat for the Sabbath before prayer
Provided he does not forgo praying with a congregation, but finds a later minyan

paragraphs: "p shemmakkin haadam mishshacharit metzuvveh lehosip lehakin ben-hashshemashot vekidita betanchuma: amar rab zeera: "p shemmakkin adam mishshacharit, metzuvveh sheyyosip ben-hashshemashot, shenneemar: "lechem mishneh"; ayyen sham. vezakur lattob ateret rashe adoni abi zlh"h, shehaya minhago lehakin besop hayyom, lemallot qearot bemine metiqa umine perot sheyyannichum al hashshulchan bisuda rishona delel-shabbat, shehaya minhago hattob leharbot beelleh al hashshulchan likbod shabbat. vetzarik kol adam leyached lo ezeh hakana laasotah likbod shabbat besop hayyom, qodem sheyyelek lebet hakkeneset lehitpallel. vaana abeda, minhagi letaqqen nerot shabbat samuk lehadlaqatam.

clarification.explanation: Even though a person prepares the needs of the Sabbath from the morning, it is a commandment to add further preparation also at twilight, as it is said, "double bread." Rabbi Yosef Chaim's father was accustomed, at the end of the day, to fill bowls with sweets and fruits to place on the table for the Sabbath night, to increase the honor of the Sabbath. Every person should set aside some preparation of his own for the honor of the Sabbath at the end of the day, before going to the synagogue, and Rabbi Yosef Chaim's own custom was to arrange the Sabbath candles close to the time of lighting them.
takeaways: Further preparation for the honor of the Sabbath is added also at twilight
One sets aside some particular preparation for the end of the day, before going to the synagogue

paragraphs: Apillu im yesh laadam kamma mesharetim babbayit leshammesho, yizzaher laasot hu beatzmo ezeh shimmush likbod shabbat. deameru baggemara: rab chisda mechattek yaraq, verabba verab yosep mebaqqeim etzim verabbi zera madliq esh, verabbi abahu nopeach bemappucha, verab pappa gadel petilot, verab nachman metaqqen habbayit. vekatab harab "machaziq beraka" za"l beshem seper hakkavvanot yashan, dehazzea shehaadam mazzia beisqe tzareke-shabbat, hqb"h mocheq bo kol haavonot kemo haddemaot; yeuyyan sham. vezakur lattob adoni harab mv"r abi zlh"h, shehaya noheg bekol ereb-shabbat lelek lashshuq lemaqom shemmokerim perot, liqnot perot letzorek shabbat, vehu haya borer umannicha letok hammoznayim shel hachenvani, veaach"k yissa hamsharet et happerot vibiem labbayit.

clarification.explanation: Even if a person has many servants in his house, he should be careful to personally do some task for the honor of the Sabbath — as we find in the Talmud that great Amoraim would cut vegetables, chop wood, light fires, and the like, with their own hands. The sweat a person sweats in the tasks of preparing for the Sabbath — the Holy One, blessed be He, erases all his sins through it, like tears. Rabbi Yosef Chaim's father was accustomed to go himself to the market to select fruits for the Sabbath and place them on the grocer's scale.
takeaways: Every person personally performs some task for the honor of the Sabbath, even if he has servants
The sweat of preparing for the Sabbath erases sins

paragraphs: Tzarik lehashchiz hassakkin bekol ereb shabbat, dehaki tanya besipre: "veyadata ki shalom aholeka" - zo hashchazat sakkin, veyalep lah middiktib: "vehekinu et asher yabiu", denirmaz hassakkin betebot "et" milleshon: "leittim ulemazmerot". vezehu mikkebod shabbat shemmakkin atzmo laakila. velaken amar alah: "ki shalom ahallek", sheim lo yashchiz hassakkin veqeha habbarzel shello yukal lachtok en kan shelom bayit, vekannizkar b"roqeach"; yeuyyan sham. vahagam ki dabar zeh neemar lepi minhag rob hammeqomot shetztzerikin lassakkin bishat seuda - hen letzorek hallechem, hen letzorek habbasar - veyesh meqomot sheen tzerikim kol-kak sakkin, mikkol maqom, kevan deyatza haddabar mippi rz"l, vesameku oto al hakkatub - tzarik lizzaher bazeh bekol hammeqomot, ki i epshar shello yitztareku lesakkin bishbil perot.

clarification.explanation: It is a commandment to sharpen the knife every eve of the Sabbath, as the Sages expounded on "and you shall know that your tent is at peace" — this refers to sharpening the knife, for if one does not sharpen the knife and cannot cut, there is no peace in the home. Although this was said according to the custom of most places that need a knife at the meal for bread and meat, and there are places that do not need it as much — since it came from the mouth of the Sages and they based it on the verse, one must be careful about this everywhere, since a knife will certainly be needed for fruit.
takeaways: The knife is sharpened every eve of the Sabbath, for the sake of peace in the home and the honor of the Sabbath

paragraphs: Lepi daat rabbenu haari"y za"l: kol tzareke shabbat yiqneh beyom shishshi, kede shettachul alehem qedushshat shabbat; mihu, im yireh shehayyom qatzar, veyesh debarim shetztzerikim tiqqun harbeh; veim yiqneh otam beyom shishshi, lo yihyeh lahem penay letaqqenam, muttar liqnot beyom chamishi. velaken, "p shehabbasar tzarik liqnoto beyom shishshi, im kol zeh, haqqereb sheqqorin bearbe pg'h (qirbe baqar), shetztzerika tiqqun veeseq harbeh, yukal liqnot beyom chamishi, kede sheyyetaqqenum veyinqom beyom chamishi; abal apiyyat happat shehu iqqar seudat shabbat, vadday tzarik leepot beyom shishshi. vaapillu mi sheddarko liqnot pat min hashshuq bekol yom, im kol zeh, pat shabbat yeapeh bebeto kede shettotzi ishto challa min haissa, vedabar beitto mah tob; lepi shebbeereb shabbat nibra adam harishon shehu challato shel olam, ubo bayyom naasa mah shennaasa; velaken yesh nashim nohagim latet perutot litzdaqa qodem haprashat chala, veqodem hadlaqat ner shabbat, veqodem tebilat metzuvveh; vesimanam: "channa" shehu: challa, nidda, hadlaqa.

clarification.explanation: According to the Ari, all the needs of the Sabbath should be bought on the sixth day (Friday), so that the holiness of the Sabbath rests upon them. But if the day is short and there are things requiring much preparation and work (such as beef innards), it is permitted to buy them on Thursday so there will be time to prepare them. But the bread, which is the main part of the Sabbath meal, must be baked on Friday; and even one who is accustomed to buying bread from the market should bake the Sabbath bread at home so that his wife can separate challah. Some women are accustomed to give a coin to charity before separating challah, before lighting the candle, and before immersion (mnemonic "Chanah": challah, niddah, hadlakah).
takeaways: The needs of the Sabbath are bought on Friday; items requiring much preparation are bought already on Thursday
The Sabbath bread is baked at home, for the separation of challah

paragraphs: Lo yipchot mishshene tabshilin likbod shabbat; veim darko bechol bishnayim - yosip beshabbat min echad yoter lepachot; veim yabi dagim chashib tosepet chashuba. umetzuvveh litom mikkol hattabshilin beereb shabbat dabar muat; veim hu betaanit, katab "eshel abraham" za"l: toem upolet, vezokeh lachayyim haelyonim.

clarification.explanation: One should prepare no fewer than two cooked dishes in honor of the Sabbath, and if one is accustomed to two on weekdays, he should add at least one more kind for the Sabbath (and fish is considered an important addition). It is a commandment to taste a small amount from all the dishes on the eve of the Sabbath, and if one is fasting, he should taste and spit it out — and through this he merits the life of the World to Come.
takeaways: At least two cooked dishes are prepared, with an addition in honor of the Sabbath
It is a commandment to taste the dishes on the eve of the Sabbath (one who is fasting tastes and spits it out)

paragraphs: Ezra hassoper "h tiqqen leyisrael sheyyihyu mekabbesin begadim bachamishi beshabbat likbod shabbat, veen rashshain lekabbes beyom shishshi. veim mekabbesin beyom rebii, gam ken chashib likbod shabbat kemo yom chamishi, ki hatchalat hahakana leshabbat hi miyyom rebii; mah sheen ken yeme rishon, sheni, shelishi hem mishshabbat sheabera, veeno nikkar bazeh kebod shabbat; mihu, im yesh lahem hekreach barishon, sheni, shelishi let lan bah. v"p sheamarnu deen rashshain lekabbes beereb shabbat - im neensu velo kibbesu qodem, rashshain lekabbes beereb shabbat, vekan' b"matteh-yeuddeh" za"l.

clarification.explanation: Ezra the Scribe enacted that clothes be laundered on Thursday in honor of the Sabbath, and that one not launder on Friday (so as to be occupied then with the needs of the Sabbath). Laundering on Wednesday is also considered to be in honor of the Sabbath, since the preparation for the Sabbath already begins then, unlike Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday, which belong to the previous Sabbath — though laundering is necessarily permitted on those days as well. Even though one should not launder on the eve of the Sabbath, if one was prevented by circumstances and did not launder beforehand, he may launder on the eve of the Sabbath.
takeaways: Laundering in honor of the Sabbath is done on Thursday (or Wednesday), not on Friday
One who was prevented by circumstances may launder even on the eve of the Sabbath

paragraphs: Vehinneh noda middibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, dehahakanot shel hashshabbat: yesh bemachshaba, veyesh bedibbur veyesh bemaaseh. vehahakana shel hammaaseh kebar bearnu otah, shehi qeniyya vaasiyya bemaakol umishteh letzorek shabbat; veod name tiqqun nerot shabbat vekayyotze, shekkol zeh hu inyan maaseh vekannizkar leel. amenam hahakana shehi bedibbur, hinneh hu hasseder shel "choq leyisrael" hamtuqqan "p rabbenu haari"y za"l, ukebar nidpas beseper "choq leyisrael" hakkavvana shetztzarik lekavven qodem qeriat pesuqe happarasha bekol yom beseder hammilluy shel shem b"n shehem otiyyot vdhv"h, debar yom beyomo. veim neenas yom echad velo qara bo, kesheyyabo bayyom sheacharayv yiqra techilla pesuqe happarasha shel etmol shello qeraam, veaach"k yiqra seder oto hayyom; "p shelletzorek yom etmol lo yoil lo, dealayv neemar: "meuvvat lo yukal litqon", im kol zeh tzarik liqrot pesuqe tora shel etmol qodem sheyyiqra seder oto hayyom, vekamporash bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar taame hammitzvot, parashat vaetchannan. vekatab harab mahara"m papiresh za"l, dehu haddin im lo qara arbaa yamim, kesheyyabo liqrot beyom chamishi, yiqra techilla haqqeria shel haarbaa yamim veaach"k seder yom chamishi; yeuyyan sham.

Veken hu haddin keshechal yv"t beemtza hashshabua, sheyyiqra bechol hammoed haqqeria tana"k shel yv"t, ki byv"t en qorin seder haqqeria shel "choq leyisrael". venistappaqti byv"t shel shabuot shebbechu"l shechal bime d' vah': ematay yiqra haqqeria shel d' vah'? velo matzati galuy lazeh; veken betisha beab shechal bachamishi, ematay yiqra haqqeria shel yom tisha beab? vididenu harab haggaon morenu rabbi eliyyahu minni nr"v amar, hu middato asa kak - shellamad belel shishshi, sheqqara techilla happesuqim shel yom chamishi miqra lebad paam achat, veacharehem lamad k"v pesuqim shel lel shishshi; veyapeh asa.

clarification.explanation: The preparations for the Sabbath (according to the Ari) are three: in action, in speech, and in thought. The preparation in action has already been explained (shopping, cooking, and preparing the candles). The preparation in speech is the daily reading order of "Chok LeYisrael," in which one reads the verses of the parasha. If one was prevented one day and did not read, when he comes the next day he should first read yesterday's parasha verses and then that day's order — even though it will not help for yesterday. Likewise, if he did not read for several days, he should make them up before reading that day's portion; and when a festival falls in the middle of the week (on which the daily order is not read), he should make up the Scripture reading of the festival during the intermediate days. Before reading the parasha verses each day, one should have in mind the order of filling in the Name "Ben" (the letters vav-dalet-heh-vav), day by day. Regarding Shavuot falling outside the Land of Israel on a Wednesday or Thursday, and likewise the Ninth of Av falling on a Thursday — Rabbi Yosef Chaim raised the question of when to read the portions for those days and found no explicit source for it; Rabbi Eliyahu Mani, on his own judgment, was accustomed to read on Friday night first the verses of Thursday (Scripture only, once) and afterward the twenty-six verses of Friday night, and he did well.
takeaways: The preparation for the Sabbath: in action, in speech, and in thought
In speech — the daily order of "Chok LeYisrael"; missed days are made up

paragraphs: Biklal hahakana shel haddibbur hannizkar hu liqrot belel shishshi achar chatzot beashmoret k"v pesuqim hannidpasim beseper "choq leyisrael"; velo yiqra hattargum, ella miqra bilbad, veyiqraem paam achat velo yikpol. veim yodea beatzmo beberur sheachar sheyyashan lo yihyeh neor qodem alot hashshachar kede liqrot k"v pesuqim hannizkarim, az yiqra otam qodem sheyyishan bitchillat hallayla; veim neenas velo lamad k"v pesuqim hannizkarim ballayla ukebar heir hayyom, im kol zeh yilmod otam babboqer; v"p sheheir hayyom, yelammedem miqra bilbad belo targum. vekatab li harab haggaon morenu rabbi eliyyahu minni nr"v, denitpashshet hamminhag beir haqqodesh tibbaneh vetikkonen, deim lo lamad k"v pesuqim ballayla, sheomer otam paam achat miqra qodem qeriat shmv"t.

clarification.explanation: Part of the preparation of speech is to read, on Friday night after midnight (in the night watch), the twenty-six verses printed in "Chok LeYisrael," Scripture only without translation, once. If one knows for certain that once he falls asleep he will not wake before dawn, he should read them before sleeping at the beginning of the night; and if he was prevented by circumstances and did not study them at night, he should study them in the morning even though it is already light — Scripture only. The custom in Jerusalem is that if one did not read them at night, he says them once before reading Shnayim Mikra veEchad Targum.
takeaways: Twenty-six verses are read on Friday night after midnight, Scripture only, once
One who was prevented reads them before sleep or in the morning

paragraphs: Gam tzarik od hakana bedibbur bayyom hashshishshi beatzmo - liqrot happarasha kullah shenayim miqra veechad targum, veachar shessiyyem happarasha yikpol pasuq haacharon, veen tzarik likpol gam hattargum shello. veen qoreim hattargum bitamim, kannizkar beshaar taame hammitzvot. veim neenas velo qara happarasha shenayim miqra veechad targum beyom shishshi, yiqraenna shenayim miqra veechad targum beyom shabbat achar hattepilla qodem qiddush shabbat. veim chal shabbat berosh chodesh, o "sheqalim" v"zakur" v"para" v"hachodesh", tzarik lomar hahaptara shel shenayim miqra veechad targum, haptarat hashshabua hen im qore hashshenayim miqra veechad targum beyom shishshi, hen im qoreah beyom shabbat atzmo.

Veda ki chaqarti bs"d: meachar ki qeriat seder "choq leyisrael" bekol yom, uqeriat k"v pesuqim lel shishshi hu bishbil hakana leshabbat bedibbur; im ken, keshechal etzlenu shabbat-bereshit beyom isru chag, denimtza shello lamedu beparashat bereshit bishbil hahakana appe' limmud shel yom echad, vegam et k"v pesuqim gam ken lo lamedu; im ken, ek naaset hahakana shel oto shabbat? vekatabti chaqira zo leharab haggaon morenu rabbi eliyyahu minni nr"v, veheshib: moda lebenah, demah shetztzarik hakana, hu kesheshsholetim yeme hachol shehem hassitra-achara, deaz tzerikin laasot hakana lehamshik qedushshat shabbat lishte toaliyyot: haachat, limshok qedushshat shabbat lanu, lesayyaenu shello yishletu alenu yeme hachol beetzem; vehashshenit, kede leqabbel hearat shabbat behadragot, velo latzet bepaam achat mechasheka leorah; amenam keshehu yv"t sheen shelita, en tzarik hakana; ad kan debarayv nr"v.

clarification.explanation:
Another preparation of speech, on Friday itself, is to read the entire parasha as Shnayim Mikra veEchad Targum, repeating the last verse (but not repeating its translation), and the translation is not read with the cantillation. If one was prevented and did not read on Friday, he should read on the Sabbath, after the prayer, before Kiddush. When the Sabbath falls on Rosh Chodesh or on one of the four special portions (Shekalim, Zachor, Parah, HaChodesh), he also reads the haftarah of the week as Shnayim Mikra veEchad Targum, whether he reads it on Friday or on the Sabbath itself.
The Ben Ish Chai raised a question: the daily reading of "Chok LeYisrael" and the reading of the twenty-six verses on Friday night are meant for the preparation of the Sabbath in speech; if so, when the Sabbath of parashat Bereshit falls on the day after a festival ("Issru Chag"), when no study of parashat Bereshit was done at all for preparation — not even one day's study, and the twenty-six verses were not said either — through what is the preparation of that Sabbath accomplished?
He asked this question to the Gaon Rabbi Eliyahu Mani, who answered: the preparation is needed specifically at a time when the weekdays are dominant, which represent the "other side" (the forces of impurity) — at such a time preparation is needed to draw down the holiness of the Sabbath, for two benefits: first, to draw the holiness of the Sabbath upon us so that it helps us so that the weekdays not dominate over us; and second, to receive the illumination of the Sabbath gradually, and not emerge all at once from darkness to light. But when a festival precedes the Sabbath (as with Issru Chag), when the weekdays have no dominance, no preparation is needed at all, and therefore there is no deficiency in that Sabbath.
takeaways: The preparation of speech on Friday: reading the entire parasha as Shnayim Mikra veEchad Targum and repeating the last verse (without its translation, and without cantillation for the translation); one who was prevented reads on the Sabbath before Kiddush
A Sabbath on Rosh Chodesh or one of the four special portions: the haftarah is also read as Shnayim Mikra veEchad Targum (on Friday or the Sabbath)

The Ben Ish Chai's question: when the Sabbath of Bereshit falls on Issru Chag and no preparation study was done at all — through what is the preparation accomplished? Rabbi Eliyahu Mani's answer: preparation is needed only when the weekdays are dominant (the "other side"), to draw down the Sabbath's holiness gradually; but when a festival precedes it, with no such dominance, no preparation is needed

paragraphs: Achar shebbearnu hahakana shel haddibbur nebaer hahakana shel hammachashaba; vehu, sheyyakin atzmo bemachshabto leqabbel or tosepet shabbat, ubeken yihyeh biklal "vehitqaddishtem, vihyitem qedoshim". utechillat hahakana hu miyyom rebii beshabua, sheyyakin atzmo bemachshabto sheyyehe rauy umukan leqabbel tosepet hannepesh mishshabbat habbaa; ubeyom chamishi yekavven lehakin atzmo sheyyihyeh rauy tosepet rucha mishshabbat habbaa; ubayyom hashshishshi yekavven lehakin atzmo sheyyihyeh rauy umukan leqabbel tosepet neshama mishshabbat habbaa. umittaam zeh lo hayu anshe mishmar mitannim beyom shishshi, mippene kebod hashshabbat; perush, kede leqabbel tosepet nishmat hashshabbat. ak beyom rishon beshabua yekavven shehu mukan lehasharat bechinat tosepet neshama mishshabbat sheabar, ki beyom rishon yishshaer cheleq mittosepet neshama shel shabbat; velaken anshe mishmar lo hayu mitannim beyom rishon, ki tzarik lehamshik bayyom hahu qetzat qedushshat neshama umenucha veoneg shabbat; ak zeh hacheleq hannishar beyom rishon yistalleq tekep behatchalat lel sheni, vetosepet harucha nishar ad sop yom sheni. vetzarik lekavven beyom sheni lihyot mukan leqabbel hasharat cheleq tosepet harucha, vetosepet hannepesh nisheret ad sop yom shelishi veaach"k tistalleq; velaken beyom shelishi yekavven lihyot mukan leqabbel hasharat cheleq tosepet hannepesh. velaken im lo hibdil bemotzae-shabbat, mabdil veholek ad yom shelishi, veraq lo yebarek beshem umalkut mishshum sapeq berakot lehaqel.

clarification.explanation: The preparation in thought is that one prepare himself mentally to receive the light of the additional measure of the Sabbath. From Wednesday he should intend to be ready to receive the additional measure of nefesh (the lower soul-level); on Thursday, the additional measure of ruach (spirit); and on Friday, the additional measure of neshamah (higher soul). From the previous Sabbath, the additional measure of neshamah remains until Sunday, the additional measure of ruach until Monday, and the additional measure of nefesh until Tuesday — and therefore one should intend each day to be ready to receive what remains. For this reason the members of the priestly watch did not fast on the eve of the Sabbath or on Sunday. And for this reason, one who did not perform Havdalah at the conclusion of the Sabbath may perform it until Tuesday, but without mentioning God's name and sovereignty (relying on the rule that we are lenient in a doubt concerning blessings).
takeaways: We prepare ourselves in thought to receive the additional measure of nefesh-ruach-neshamah of the Sabbath
One who did not perform Havdalah may do so until Tuesday, without God's name and sovereignty

paragraphs: Tob lepannot qure akkabish shebbabbayit bekol ereb shabbat qodesh kede legaresh haqqelippa. vekatab harab "kap hachayyim" za"l mippi hashshemua, denakon lepannot zeh qodem chatzot davqa.

clarification.explanation: It is good to clear away spider webs in the house every eve of the holy Sabbath, in order to drive away the kelipah (the force of impurity). It is proper to do this specifically before midday.
takeaways: Spider webs are cleared away on the eve of the Sabbath, and it is proper to do so before midday

paragraphs: Hagam demin haddin mistapperin kol hayyom vaapillu misseper yisrael - tob veyashar lehistapper qodem chatzot; ki rabbenu haari"y za"l haya maqpid lehistapper qodem chatzot, ben bechol, ben beereb shabbat qodesh. veyizzaher laqutz tzipparene yadayv veraglayv bekol ereb shabbat. veim lo yukal bekol ereb shabbat, mippene sheshshoheh giddulam, yizzaher laqutz kol shette shabbatot. vetzarik liqbor hatztzippareniyyim bebet-hakkisse betok hanneqeb, velo yizreqem kilachar yad, kede shello yitpazzeru mehem beqarqa bet-hakkisse veyidresu alehem. veim qatzatz tzipparenayv venizraq echad mehem sheeno roehu, yekabbed hammaqom hahu bemakbedet, veyizroq hazzebel beneqeb shel bet-hakkisse o baashpa. veyizzaher biqtzitzat hatztzipparenayim shello yippelu al begadayv, vekol shekken shello yaqotz veyannicha al begadayv; vetzarik lehizzaher shello yannicha hatztzippareniyyim apillu al minalayv, veen chilluq bazeh ben tzipparene yadayim leben tzipparene ragliyyim.

clarification.explanation: Even though by strict law it is permitted to get a haircut at any time during the day, it is good and proper to do so before midday, as the Ari was careful to do. One should be careful to cut the nails of his hands and feet every eve of the Sabbath, and if he cannot do so every week (because they have not grown enough), at least every two weeks. The nail clippings should be buried in the hole of the outhouse and not simply thrown away; and if one was thrown and he cannot see it, he should sweep the area and throw the debris into the hole or into the trash. One should be careful that the nail clippings do not fall on his clothes or shoes, whether from the hands or the feet.
takeaways: One gets a haircut and cuts his nails on the eve of the Sabbath, preferably before midday
The nail clippings are buried, and care is taken that they not fall on clothes or shoes

paragraphs: Metzuvveh lirchotz panayv yadayv veraglayv bemayim chammin bekol ereb shabbat; vikavven bazeh lidchot haqqelippa miyyadayv veraglayv shehem qetzavot vesop shel haggup. umetzuvveh lirchotz beborit gam ken, vikavven laasot bazeh hattiqqun shel hassika shehiyyatah noheget etzel harishonim shehayu sakin tamid; veharechitza yaaseh achar qetzitzat hatztzippareniyyim. vekatab beseper "keter-malkut", shello yirchatz raglayv beotam hammayim sherachatz bahem panayv veyadayv, ella yishpekem veyabi mayim chadashim. gam yizzaher lenaggeb panayv veyadayv bebat-achat qodem rechitzat raglayv; veachar sheyyirchatz raglayv, gam ken yizzaher lenaggebam techilla bemitpachat veaach"k yilbash minalayv; velo yilbash minalayv beodam lachim, velo yenaggebem bebigdo o bachaluqo.

clarification.explanation: It is a commandment to wash the face, hands, and feet in hot water every eve of the Sabbath, with the intention of pushing away the kelipah from the extremities. It is also a commandment to wash with soap, as a remedy corresponding to the anointing practiced by the earlier generations, after cutting the nails. One should not wash his feet in the same water used to wash his face and hands, but in fresh water, and should dry his face and hands together before washing his feet; and after washing his feet he should dry them and only then put on his shoes — he should not wear them while wet, nor dry them with his clothing.
takeaways: The face, hands, and feet are washed in hot water and with soap on the eve of the Sabbath
Separate water is used for the feet, and one dries off before putting on shoes

paragraphs: Mah tob umah naim al pi hassod litbol beereb shabbat, kede leqabbel tosepet nepesh rucha uneshama delel-shabbat "y tebila. utebila rishona, letahora mikkol tuma; usheniyya, letiqqun avon hakkaas; ushelishit, lehapshit bigde chol meal hannepesh; urebiit, lehasir ulehapshit mealayv harucha shehaya shora alayv bime hachol, kede sheyyishreh alayv atta rucha mibberia; vezeh yihyeh "y hy"h bemilluy hahin kazeh: ale"p h"h yu"d h"h, vikavven bo bitbila zo; vachamishit hi likbod hashshabbat leqabbel tosepet veheara shel qedushshat hashshabbat. veyesh nohagin litbol shelosha tebilot, keneged: nepesh, rucha, neshama; veyesh nohagin chamishsha, keneged: nepesh, rucha, neshama, chayya, yechida.

Vegam beyom shabbat babboqer qodem tepillat shacharit tob veyapeh meod litbol, kede leqabbel tosepet nepesh rucha uneshama deyom shabbat; ki tosepet nepesh rucha uneshama shel hayyom hem gedolim yoter mishshel layla, shehem bechinat dukera. veim shimmesh mittato belel-shabbat, yitbol babboqer shettayim: achat, lehaabir rucha tuma; vehashsheniyya, leqabbel tosepet shabbat shel hayyom. venireh li: "p shello shimmesh, gam ken nakon litbol shettayim, ki ulay nitma battippa qetanna behishtanna, velav addateh. veharab haggaon morenu rabbi eliyyahu manni nr"v katab li: minhag hachasidim beir haqqodesh tvbb" litbol beshacharit shel shabbat shettayim: haachat, lehaabir rucha hattuma; vehashsheniyya, leqabbel tosepet shabbat kipshat dibre rabbenu za"l. veyesh nohagin litbol beqabbalat tosepet shabbat chamishsha, keneged perate nepesh, rucha, neshama, chayya, yechida; veyesh mosipin od shettayim keneged chayya vichida diklalut; ad kan debarayv nr"v.

clarification.explanation: It is very good, according to the esoteric tradition, to immerse on the eve of the Sabbath, to receive the additional measure of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah of the Sabbath night. There are five immersions: for purification from all impurity; for the repair of the sin of anger; to strip off the weekday garments from the soul; to remove the spirit that rested upon him during the weekdays; and to receive the additional holiness of the Sabbath. The fourth immersion, which removes and strips away from the person the "spirit" that rested upon him during the weekdays so that a spirit from a new creation may rest upon him, is performed with the intention of the Name "Ehyeh" in the spelling with the letters heh-heh — alef, heh, heh, yud, heh, heh. Some are accustomed to immerse three times (corresponding to nefesh, ruach, neshamah), and some five times. It is also good and proper to immerse on Sabbath morning before the morning prayer, since the additional measure of the day is greater than that of the night. If one had relations on Sabbath night, he should immerse twice in the morning (once to remove the spirit of impurity and once for the addition of the Sabbath), and it is proper to immerse twice even if he did not have relations. The custom of the pious ones in Jerusalem is to immerse twice on Sabbath morning.
takeaways: One immerses on the eve of the Sabbath (three or five immersions) to receive the additional holiness
In the fourth immersion (which removes the weekday "spirit") one has in mind the Name Ehyeh in the heh-heh spelling
It is also good to immerse on Sabbath morning; after relations, one immerses twice

paragraphs: Lepi daat rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot, tzarik lizzaher shello yenaggeb atzmo bemitpachat kesheyyaaleh mehattebila, ki mime shabbat, tzarik shehaggup yishab otam; mihu, nireh li: kevan sheddabar zeh eno meakkeb beiqqar hammitzva vehattiqqun shel hattebila, hinneh kol adam asher yiqsheh alayv dabar hazzeh laasoto mitztzad mizgo, eno tzarik lehizzaher bekak; dela mibbaya bimot hachorep asher hemma mukrachim lenaggeb mechamat haqqerirut, ella apillu bimot haqqayitz yesh bene-adam sheen yekolim lehishshaer beli niggub. al-ken nireh li, mi sheddabar zeh qasheh alayv, yenaggeb kol gupo, veraq yishshaer maqom echad begupo belo niggub, vetob sheyyashir zerootayv.

clarification.explanation: According to the Ari in Sha'ar HaKavanot, one should be careful not to dry the body with a towel when emerging from the immersion, so that the body absorbs the water of the Sabbath. But since this does not invalidate the essential fulfillment of the commandment, one for whom this is difficult due to his constitution need not be careful about it — not only in winter, but even in summer there are those who cannot remain undried. Therefore, one for whom this is difficult should dry his whole body and leave only one place undried, and it is good that he leave his arms undried.
takeaways: According to the Ari, one does not fully dry off after the eve-of-Sabbath immersion
One for whom this is difficult should dry everything and leave one place undried (such as the arms)

paragraphs: Yizzaher leyached begadim neqiyyim vetobim likbod shabbat; vehaolam lo nahagu bekak leyached leshabbat hechaluq vehammiknasayim; mihu, hannizhar bazeh, tabo alayv beraka. venoda, ki rabbenu haari"y za"l haya nizhar bazeh, vehizhir et rabbenu harab chayyim veyittol za"l, kesheyyilbash hachilluq shel shabbat beereb shabbat, lekavven beshem qadosh "ziharayya-l", vekavvana zo moelet lehamshik haqqedushsha elayv. veyizzaher kol adam shello yilbash begadim shechorim beshabbat; vaapillu obere derakim yizzaharu shello lilbosh bigde chol ubegadim shechorim beshabbat, gam beodam badderek, sheshshobetim bepundaq o bammidbar o bispina; veotam hannohagim lilbosh betok y"b chodesh shel ab vaem bigde chol vegam shechorim beshabbatot vy"t, toin hem veissura abedi. vezakur lattob ateret rashe adoni harab mv"r abi za"l, shehaya machlip begadayv beshabbatot vy"t betok y"b chodesh shel abiv veimmo. veken asinu maaseh betok y"b chodesh shel adoni abi zlh"h, deachar happetira bechodesh echad hechelapnu ani vaachi habbegadim beshabbat, velo labashnu begadim haiqqarim shel shabbat, ella asinu begadim chadashim metuqqanim leshabbatot shel otah hashshana. veken asinu betok y"b chodesh shel adonati immi tntzb"h. veayyen "birke-yosep", yoreh dea, siman t', veayyen beshulchan aruk, yoreh dea, siman shpt, seip g'; yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: One should be careful to set aside clean, good clothes in honor of the Sabbath, and one who is careful to set aside even a robe and trousers specifically for the Sabbath — blessing will come upon him (and so the Ari was accustomed). Every person should be careful not to wear black clothes on the Sabbath, even travelers who rest at an inn, in the wilderness, or on a ship. Those accustomed to wearing weekday and black clothes on the Sabbath and festivals during the year of mourning for a father or mother are mistaken and commit a transgression; Rabbi Yosef Chaim's father would change his clothes on the Sabbath and festivals during his year of mourning, and Rabbi Yosef Chaim himself did the same (with new, proper clothes prepared for the Sabbaths of that year).
takeaways: Fine clothes are set aside for the Sabbath, and black is not worn
Even a mourner within the year changes his clothes for the Sabbath and festivals

paragraphs: Bekol ereb shabbat qodesh haya minhago shel rabbenu haari"y za"l leqayyem mitzvat erube chatzerot veshittupe meboot; umebarek al happat birkat haerub, veomer "bedin eruba veku'", umezakkeh libne hechatzer "y adam acher, ukemo shekkatab beseper hakkavvanot, dap tz"b, ammud g; yeuyyan sham. upoh irenu bagdad y", anachnu osim erub zeh mishshana leshana bematztza hakkeshera lechag hammatztzot; utehillot lael sheyyesh lanu zekut bimtzuvva zo, shennaasa haerub mishshellanu venizkeh lekol bene hair hazzot, veen reshut leshum adam zulatenu laasot hammitzva hannizkeret, ki hi ittanu nachalat abot mizzeman ateret rashe harab haggaon mv"r zeqeni rabbenu mosheh chayyim zlh"h. vehamminhag lehannicha haerub hannizkar bebet-hakkeneset haggedola.

clarification.explanation: Every eve of the holy Sabbath the Ari was accustomed to fulfill the commandment of eiruvei chatzerot and shitufei mevo'ot: he would recite the blessing over the bread for the eiruv, say "With this eiruv," and grant a share to the residents of the courtyard through another person. In Baghdad this eiruv is renewed every year with matzah kosher for Passover, and it is made by Rabbi Yosef Chaim, granting a share to all the residents of the city — an inheritance from his ancestors since the time of his grandfather — and no one else has permission to make it. The eiruv is placed in the Great Synagogue.
takeaways: The commandment of eiruvei chatzerot and shitufei mevo'ot is fulfilled every eve of the Sabbath
In Baghdad, an annual eiruv is made with matzah, and Rabbi Yosef Chaim grants a share in it to the whole city

paragraphs: Asur laasot melaka beereb shabbat min zeman mincha qetanna ulemala, shehu tesha shaot umechetza, beshaot zemanniyyot. v"p sheyyesh soberim leesor min zeman mincha gedola - qayma lan halaka kedibre hammaqqel bedibre soperim. velo aseru ella melaka gemura, abal peraqmatya mutteret. veap al gab deyesh machmirim gam bazeh, mikkol maqom pashat hamminhag behetter bekol hammeqomot. veha dimlaka gemura asura, haynu beqobea atzmo aleha, abal im hi lepi shaa, derek aray, muttar; ukeha ditnan (shabbat yz:): bet shammay omerim, en shorin deyo vesammanin vekarshinin, ella kede sheyyishshoru mibbeod yom, ubet hillel mattirin. velaken yesh lehazhir bazeh toperim vechayyatim veoregin unegarim vetzorepim, sheqqibbuin laasot melaaktam; veken gam soperim haqqibbuin limleket hassapparut shel st"m tzerikin lehizzaher; abal hakkoteb separim leatzmo derek limmudo, shari, apillu qobea atzmo, vaapillu sheeno koteb debar chiddush, kevan shehu tzorek metzuvveh, shari, vekannizkar bapposeqim za"l. veiggeret shelomim, shari; veken yesh lehattir apillu ketibat iggeret shel peraqmatya, vaapillu sheeno dabar haabed; veayyen behilkot chvh"m, siman tqmh. veken yesh lehattir liktob cheshbonotayv velachshob hotzaotayv kedin chvh"m, vekol shekken hu; mihu, cheshbon hakkatub etzlo bepinqas hayyome verotzeh lesidro bepinqas acher, asur; veayyen "mg"" za"l v"eliyya raba", siman tqmh.

Veken im ba lo cheshbon mechabero meir acheret, verotzeh lehatiqo bepinqaso, asur, deen zeh dabar haabed, deepshar lehatiq achar shabbat. umi shehu ani veoseh melaka kede lehotzi hassakar letzorek shabbat, muttar, apillu deyesh lo belav haki kede mayim velechem, im en lo leanneg basar o dagim, shari. veayyen "mishbetzot zahab", siman rn. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" heeleti, deim hu hekin babboqer behalvaa bishbil oneg-shabbat basar vekayyotze, al semak hassakar sheyyihyeh lo beereb-shabbat bimlakto sheoseq bah kol hayyom, shari leh laasoq kol hayyom, deim teesor lo, lo yakin babboqer behalvaa.

clarification.explanation:
It is forbidden to do work on the eve of the Sabbath from the time of Minchah Ketanah (nine and a half seasonal hours) onward. Only completed work that one sets himself to do steadily is forbidden, but commerce is permitted, as is occasional, incidental work. Therefore tailors, weavers, carpenters, goldsmiths, and scribes of sacred texts who are regularly occupied in their craft must be careful, but one who writes for his own study is permitted (since it serves a commandment), and it is likewise permitted to write a letter of greeting, a business letter, and to calculate one's accounts and expenses, as on the intermediate days of a festival.
Nevertheless, an account already written in one's daily notebook that he wishes to copy and arrange into another notebook is forbidden; likewise, if an account comes to him from a colleague in another city and he wishes to copy it into his notebook, this is forbidden, since this is not "a matter that will be lost" — for it can be copied after the Sabbath.
A poor person who does work in order to earn wages for the sake of delighting in the Sabbath is permitted to do so, even if he already has water and bread, provided he has no other way to delight in the Sabbath with meat or fish. The Ben Ish Chai (in Makbetzal) added: one who prepared meat or the like in the morning, on credit, for the delight of the Sabbath, relying on the wages he would earn that day from his work, in which he is occupied all day — he is permitted to work all day; for if this were forbidden, he would not prepare on credit in the morning, and would end up losing the delight of the Sabbath. Although some hold that it is forbidden already from the time of Minchah Gedolah, the halachah follows the lenient opinion in matters of rabbinic law; and although some are stringent even regarding commerce, the widespread custom everywhere is to permit it.
takeaways: Completed work one sets himself to do is forbidden from the time of Minchah Ketanah on the eve of the Sabbath; commerce and occasional work are permitted; writing for one's own study, letters of greeting or business, and calculating expenses are permitted

But copying an account (from one's own notebook to another, or one received from a colleague in another city) is forbidden, since it is not "a matter that will be lost" (it can wait until after the Sabbath)

A poor person doing work for the delight of the Sabbath (meat/fish) is permitted; even one who prepared it in the morning on credit, relying on that day's wages, may work all day (Makbetzal), since otherwise he would lose the delight of the Sabbath

paragraphs: Asur liqboa beereb shabbat seuda gedola shel mishteh sheeno ragil bah bime hachol, apillu babboqer, mippene kebod hashshabbat. bammeh debarim amurim? bisudat hareshut, o apillu seudat mitzva, ella sheen zemannah mukrach lihyot oto hayyom, shehu yakol lidchotah achar shabbat; abal seudat mitzva shezzemannah oto hayyom, kegon seudat mila useudat erusin venissuin, muttar; "p sheal yede kak lo yukal leekol seudat shabbat ballayla leteabon kol kak - en bekak kelum; mihu, yizzaher shettihyeh qodem shaa asirit, vekol mah sheepshar lo lehaqdim, yaqdim. useudat bar mitzva - im hu mammash bayyom shennaasa bar mitzva, dinah kisudat mila; veken seudat pidyon habben bizmanno, dehaynu beyom sheloshim veechad leleda, shari.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to hold a large festive meal on the eve of the Sabbath, of a kind one is not accustomed to on weekdays, even in the morning, out of respect for the Sabbath — this applies to an optional meal or even to a meal of a commandment that could be postponed until after the Sabbath. But a meal of a commandment whose time is specifically that day (a circumcision, a betrothal, a wedding) is permitted, even though one will then not eat at night with full appetite, provided it takes place before the tenth hour, and the earlier the better. A bar mitzvah meal on the day the boy becomes bar mitzvah has the same law as a circumcision meal, as does the redemption of the firstborn at its proper time (the thirty-first day).
takeaways: A large festive meal is not held on the eve of the Sabbath
A meal of a commandment whose time is that specific day is permitted, preferably before the tenth hour

paragraphs: Seuda sheragil bah bime hachol, dehaynu seuda qetanna sheenah shel mishteh, muttar min haddin leakelah kol hayyom, abal metzuvveh lehimmana mizzeh mittechillat shaa asirit, kede sheyyokal seudat hallayla shel shabbat leteabon. veleekol velishtot beli qebiut seuda, eno nimna ad qabbalat-shabbat, umikkol maqom, hammachmir gam bazeh tabo alayv beraka.

clarification.explanation: A small meal of the kind one is accustomed to on weekdays (not a festive one) is permitted by strict law throughout the day, but it is a commandment to refrain from it starting from the tenth hour, in order to eat the Sabbath night meal with appetite. Eating and drinking without a formal meal is not restricted until the acceptance of the Sabbath, but one who is stringent even about this — blessing will come upon him.
takeaways: One refrains from a small meal from the tenth hour, in order to eat at night with appetite
Casual eating is permitted until the acceptance of the Sabbath

paragraphs: Kol taanit yachid sheen qabua lo zeman, sheyyukal lehitannot beezeh yom sheyyirtzeh, en mitanneh beereb shabbat; abal im zemanno beereb shabbat, kegon taanit yartzayt, o taanit shiba baadar, o taanit ereb rosh chodesh, muttar lehitannot beereb shabbat, ak lo yashlim ad tzet hakkokabim; viqabbel otam meiqqara addata dehaki; veraq asara betebet shechal beereb shabbat, tzarik lehashlim ad tzet hakkokabim. vetob lomar bekol ereb shabbat qodem qabbalat shabbat shir-hashshirim besimcha ubeqol naim.

clarification.explanation: Any personal fast that has no fixed date is not observed on the eve of the Sabbath. But a fast whose time is specifically the eve of the Sabbath (a yahrzeit, the Seventh of Adar, the eve of Rosh Chodesh) may be observed, but one should not complete it until the emergence of the stars, and should accept it from the outset with this intention. Only the Tenth of Tevet, when it falls on the eve of the Sabbath, must be completed until the emergence of the stars. It is good to recite the Song of Songs with joy and in a pleasant voice every eve of the Sabbath, before accepting the Sabbath.
takeaways: A fast is observed on the eve of the Sabbath only if its date is fixed for that day, and it is not completed until night
The Tenth of Tevet is completed; the Song of Songs is recited before accepting the Sabbath
